name: opening_range_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The classic 15-minute Opening Range Breakout (ORB) captures the directional resolution of early-session uncertainty. The first 15 minutes (09:15-09:30 IST) establish a range as institutional pre-market orders, overnight gap adjustments, and global cue reactions settle. A breakout above/below this range with volume signals the session's directional bias. The edge exists because the opening range concentrates information discovery into a narrow time window — once resolved, the chosen direction tends to persist for 1-3 hours. The Indian market opens 15 min later than pre-market (09:00), so the 09:15-09:30 range absorbs the most intense order flow. The inefficiency persists because while ORB is well-known, proper execution with volume confirmation and tight risk management is the differentiator.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents on NSE + NIFTY 50 index futures
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND opening_range(15min) > 0.3% AND < 2.0%

conditions: volume on breakout bar > SUM(volume, 15) / 15 * 2.0 (2x avg first-15-min bar volume)
long.confirmation: first 1-min close above OR_high with body > 50% of bar range (not a wick breakout)

short.confirmation: first 1-min close below OR_low with body > 50% of bar range

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout bar close

exit.target: 1.0 * OR_range from breakout level (measured move equal to OR range)
exit.stop_loss: OR_mid (midpoint of opening range) — if price retreats to OR midpoint, breakout failed
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * OR_range once profit exceeds 0.7 * OR_range
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back inside OR for 3 consecutive bars (false breakout confirmed)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; scale down if OR_range > 1.5% (larger range = larger risk)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; ORB works best in moderate vol environments (14-22)
filters.time_filter: entry only after 09:30 IST; no new entries after 12:00
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume > 2x average first-15-min bar volume
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakout direction aligned with global cue (SGX Nifty direction pre-market)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy day (ORB unreliable on event-driven volatility)
other_filters: OR_range must be between 0.3% and 2.0% — too narrow is noise, too wide means stop is too far
only trade first breakout attempt — if price breaks, comes back, and breaks again, skip

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — ORB is well-known but consistent execution with proper filters is rare

weaknesses: False breakouts are the primary failure mode — price breaks OR, triggers entry, then reverses into the range
ORB works best in trending markets; in range-bound, choppy days, both sides of the OR get hit (double loss)
The first breakout after OR is often the most crowded trade — many traders use ORB, reducing edge from crowding
prior_art: Opening Range Breakout is one of the oldest day trading strategies (Toby Crabel, 1990 'Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns'). Mark Fisher's ACD method is a variation. Extremely well-documented. Indian adaptation by Zerodha Varsity and multiple trading educators. The 15-min variant is the most common in India due to the 09:15 market open.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 70bps - 0.50 * 39bps = 35 - 19.5 = 15.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4.5 bps per trade. Positive. ORB is one of the more viable strategies despite being well-known, because: (1) few traders execute it with proper filters, (2) the measured move target is disciplined, (3) the OR midpoint stop is logical and prevents catastrophic losses.
